column1: What did you learn about money from the adults in your childhood home?
column2: Which of those lessons do you still follow?

column1: What was your first memory of earning your own money?
column2: What did you do with it?

column1: Where do you fall between spender and saver by nature?
column2: Where do you think that tendency comes from?

column1: What does having enough mean to you?
column2: How would you know when you had reached it?

column1: What is the best money you have ever spent?
column2: What made it worth every penny?

column1: What is a purchase you regret?
column2: What did it teach you about what you value?

column1: How did your family talk about money at the dinner table?
column2: How do you talk about it now?

column1: What is something you will happily splurge on?
column2: What does it give you that is worth the cost?

column1: What is something you refuse to spend much on?
column2: What makes it not worth it to you?

column1: Who is the most generous person you know?
column2: What does their generosity look like?

column1: What does generosity mean to you beyond money?
column2: How do you practice it?

column1: What money habit are you proudest of?
column2: How did you build it?

column1: What would you do with an unexpected windfall of a thousand dollars?
column2: What does that choice say about your priorities?

column1: What would you do differently with money if you were starting over at twenty?
column2: What would you keep the same?

column1: How do you feel about lending money to friends or family?
column2: What experience shaped that feeling?

column1: What is a time you felt rich without having much money?
column2: What made you feel that way?

column1: What does financial security feel like to you?
column2: What would help you feel more of it?

column1: What is something money cannot buy that you value deeply?
column2: How do you make room for it in your life?

column1: What is a childhood treat or purchase that felt like a big deal?
column2: Why did it feel so special?

column1: How do you decide whether something is a need or a want?
column2: Where does that line get blurry for you?

column1: What is a cause you love to give to?
column2: What first connected you to it?

column1: How do you want to teach young people about money?
column2: What lesson matters most to pass on?

column1: What is the most frugal thing you are secretly proud of?
column2: Who taught you that trick?

column1: What would your ideal relationship with money look like?
column2: What is one step toward that?

column1: What experience would you rather pay for than a thing?
column2: What makes experiences worth more to you?

column1: What is a money mistake that turned out to be a good teacher?
column2: How did you recover from it?

column1: How do you think money changes people?
column2: Where have you seen that happen?

column1: What would you do with your time if money were never a concern again?
column2: How much of that could you do now?

column1: What is something you saved up for that felt amazing to finally buy?
column2: How long did it take you?

column1: How do your money values differ from your parents' values?
column2: What caused that difference?

column1: What does a rich life mean to you apart from a bank balance?
column2: Who do you know who lives that kind of life?

column1: How do you feel when someone picks up the check for you?
column2: How do you like to return the favor?

column1: What is a free pleasure that you would not trade for anything?
column2: When did you discover it?

column1: How do you handle money conversations with people you love?
column2: What makes those conversations easier?

column1: What is a dream that money would make possible for you?
column2: What would it feel like to get there?

column1: What do you think is the right amount to spend on a gift?
column2: What is a gift that felt priceless no matter its cost?

column1: What did you learn about money from your first apartment or home?
column2: What would you tell yourself back then?

column1: How do you think about comfort versus simplicity?
column2: Where do you land on that today?

column1: What is a family story about money that gets told again and again?
column2: What do you think it really says?

column1: What does wealth look like in the community you grew up in?
column2: How has your view of it changed?

column1: How do you reward yourself after a big accomplishment?
column2: What is a reward you still remember?

column1: What is something you own that you would never sell?
column2: What makes it so valuable to you?

column1: What does it mean to you to live within your means?
column2: When has that been hardest?

column1: How do you want to use money to help the people you love?
column2: What would make that feel good rather than stressful?

column1: What is the kindest thing anyone has done for you with money?
column2: How did it change things for you?

column1: What would you like to stop worrying about when it comes to money?
column2: What might help you let it go?

column1: What is something you used to want badly that no longer appeals to you?
column2: What changed your mind?

column1: How do you balance enjoying today with planning for tomorrow?
column2: Which side do you tend to lean toward?

column1: What do you think it means to be good with money?
column2: Who in your life fits that description?

column1: How have your values shaped the way you spend your time?
column2: Where do your time and money tell the same story?

column1: What would you want people to understand about your relationship with money?
column2: What experiences are behind it?

column1: What does contentment mean to you?
column2: When do you feel it most?
